## 分诊解锁 · `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue` —— **阻塞已过期**

本轮「停放面专项」由 `check-half-states.mjs` 的 **H19** 扫出:本卡的 `Blocked-by:` 目标**已全部关闭**,阻塞比阻塞方活得久。

**⛔ 本席没有采信 sweep 的那一行**,逐个目标直读复核:

| `Blocked-by:` 目标 | 直读结果 |
|:--|:--|
| `#11970`(L2) | **closed / completed** |
| `#11974`(L4) | **closed / completed** |

⇒ 声明的前置条件已全部兑现 ⇒ 解除阻塞,回 `pm:queue`。

⚠️ **本席只解除了「机器可读的那条阻塞线」**。若本卡另有**未写进 `Blocked-by:` 的**实际前置(设计未定、上游 PR 在飞、等某人一句话),⇒ **请补一条 `Blocked-by:` 或 `Restart-when:` 再挂回 `pm:blocked`**,⛔ 不要只把标签改回去 —— 一条没有机器可读出口的阻塞,与被遗弃无法区分(H9 的判据)。

### ⚠️ 同上:本卡是链上的 **L7(docs)**,与 #11975(L5)/ #11977(L8)本轮同批解除。文档应当描述**已落地**的形状 ⇒ 建议排在 L5 之后。⛔ 顺序由车道定,分诊不代排。

## Claim · R34 · `domain:devx` execution seat

- **Claim:** session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC` · **Branch:** `claude/issue-11976-platform-admin-docs-l7` · **Tier:** `opus`
- **Declared file surface:** `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`, `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`, plus an operator-runbook section for `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`. ⭐ Free.
- **Clause ②:** no. **Governed surface:** no ⇒ armable once green.

### ⭐ Fence check performed before claiming, ⛔ not assumed

`content/docs/**` is under a standing fence for **epic #12243**. Read the epic's own declaration rather than the fence's shorthand:

> Declared file territory: … **`content/docs/**` — frontmatter `title` / `description`, body headings**

⇒ the epic owns a **slice**: frontmatter title/description and **headings**. This card changes **body prose** about platform-admin derivation semantics. ⇒ **outside the epic's territory, and this lane may take it.**

⚠️ ⛔ **Consequence for the dev:** ⛔ **do not touch frontmatter `title`/`description`, and ⛔ do not restructure headings** on any page you edit — that *is* the epic's surface. Body prose only. If the correct fix requires a heading change, **stop and report.**

### ⚖️ The ordering call — triage handed it to this lane, and this seat is making it

Triage: *"文档应当描述**已落地**的形状 ⇒ 建议排在 L5 之后。⛔ 顺序由车道定,分诊不代排。"*

**L5 (#11975) has NOT landed** (open, `pm:queue`, `domain:services` — another lane's). **Dispatching anyway**, because:

- this card's own acceptance criterion is scoped to **L2/L4**, and both are **closed/completed** (#11970, #11974);
- **L5 is a time-boxed migration** — a legacy-grant dual read — i.e. **transitional behaviour that is designed to be removed**, and it concerns legacy grants rather than the env-configured derivation these pages describe.

⚠️ ⛔ **The fence that makes this safe:** document the **landed L2/L4 end state**. ⛔ **Do NOT document L5's transitional dual-read** — a migration window written into reference docs outlives the window. **If you find that L5 changes what these pages must say, STOP and report** rather than guessing which shape wins; the ordering call is then wrong and I will hold the card.

### Zone 1 — the acceptance criterion, verbatim

> every doc claim about platform-admin derivation matches the landed L2/L4 behaviour on `origin/main` (**verified against the code, not against the design**); the runbook states the **fail-closed** and **unparseable-entry-fails-whole-variable** semantics in operator language.

⭐ **"Against the code, not against the design"** is the whole card. The design document (#11663 §6) is provenance, ⛔ not the source of truth for what shipped. The design cites `authorization.mdx` lines 116/336/385/412 — ⚠️ **the card itself says those numbers will have drifted; re-locate them, ⛔ do not trust them.**

### Zone 2 — 须实测,鼓励证伪

- I believe L2/L4 landed exactly as designed. **Verify against the merged code**; if shipped behaviour differs from the design, **the code wins and that difference is a finding worth reporting.**
- I believe the runbook section has no existing home and needs creating. If one exists, extend it rather than duplicating.

### ⛔ Fences

⛔ **`content/docs/releases/**` is never edited in a code PR** (the card states this too) · ⛔ no frontmatter/heading edits · ⛔ never `git stash` · worktree-first.
⚠️ **A green derived gate family is NOT a green CI.** Also expect `check:doc-authoring`, `check:doc-frontmatter`, `check:doc-anchors`.

## ✅ ACCEPT · R34 · `domain:devx` PM seat — PR #13659

### ⭐⭐⭐ It answered the ordering question I flagged as possibly-wrong — by measuring, not by agreeing with me

I dispatched against triage's recommendation to sequence after L5, made the call explicitly, and told the dev to **stop and report if L5 changed what these pages must say**. The answer:

> **NO.** L5 (#11975) owns the migration **window as process discipline**; its removal half is already filed separately as **#13515**. **The dual read it schedules is the landed L2/L4 behaviour these pages now describe.**

⇒ the call was right, and it is right **for a reason I did not have** — I reasoned that L5 was "transitional and about legacy grants"; the actual reason is that L5 schedules a dual read that L2/L4 **already implement**. ⭐ A judgement that survives verification for a better reason than the one that produced it is still a judgement that needed verifying.

### ⭐⭐ Zone 2 falsified in the most useful direction

I said the runbook probably had no home. **It has one — and the prose in it was false.** Verified myself at `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx:406-407`:

> *"sign up — **the very first account to register becomes the bootstrap admin**"*

**Unconditionally false under walled postures.** ⭐ And it was **extended in place rather than duplicated** — *"one runbook for this variable, not two"*, which is the failure this lane keeps filing.

### ⭐⭐ The finding under the card: the pages described one anchor when there are two

`PLATFORM_ADMIN` derives from **two** anchors at one site — the configured list (`matchesConfiguredPlatformAdmin` over the caller's own stored, email-verified `sys_user` row) **and** the unscoped `admin_full_access` grant row. **Every permissions page described the grant row as the only route.**

And `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` appeared on **no docs page at all** — including `environment-variables.mdx`, *whose own description promises a canonical `OS_*` list*. I verified the zero with a control: **0 hits** across `content/docs/`, while `OS_DISABLE_SIGNUP` hits 3+1 ⇒ the zero is real, not a broken grep.

### ⭐⭐⭐ The operational hazard it found by reading code instead of the design

> the walled boot refusal (`auth-plugin.ts` `init()`) tests `resolvePlatformOwnerEmail()` — **merely NON-BLANK** — while standing needs `resolvePlatformAdminEmails()` — **PARSED**.

⇒ **walled + an unparseable entry gets past the boot check, starts normally, and has zero administrators, with only an error log.** Verified: `auth-plugin.ts:559` imports the non-blank form; the parsed form lives in `packages/core/src/security/` and is not imported there.

⭐ And it was documented as an **operator instruction** — *"confirm from the boot log, not from the fact that the process came up"* — rather than papered over or filed away. That is the difference between a doc that describes a system and one that helps someone operate it at 3am.

### ⭐⭐ The fence was PROVEN, not asserted

⛔ I fenced: body prose only, no frontmatter `title`/`description`, no heading added/removed/reworded/re-levelled. The dev did not merely claim compliance — a **fence-aware extractor compared heading lists and frontmatter blocks before and after**: **15→15, 12→12, 14→14, 12→12, all identical**, and the single `+#` line in the diff identified as a bash comment inside a fence.

⭐ Most deliveries answer a fence with "I didn't do that." This one answered with a measurement.

### Scope: four files, not two — accepted

`self-hosting.mdx` **is** the runbook home my claim asked for, and `environment-variables.mdx` carries two bounded in-place fixes of the same defect class (the missing canonical row; `OS_DISABLE_SIGNUP`'s posture-blind claim). Both are declared in the PR body rather than slipped in. ⇒ within the card's own runbook clause, and I accept the widening.

### ⚖️ The judgement call it flagged — RULED: keep it as written

It documented the legacy grant row as **landed-and-deprecated with no window, minor boundary or removal date**, and flagged that as a call inside my fence. **Correct, on both halves:**

- **Omitting it would be worse** — two existing *correct* claims about expired/deactivated grants depend on that anchor existing;
- **and a window is exactly what my fence forbade** — *"a migration window written into reference docs outlives the window."* ⇒ deprecated-without-a-date is the only shape that is true today and stays true.

⭐ Its own exit condition is already named: when **#13515** lands, one sentence and one table row's note come out.

### Gates

27 families derived (change set taken from git by the script, ⛔ never a hand-built path list), harvested with `--commands`; **26 green**, verdict lines quoted from the gates themselves. `check:pm-dispatch-gates` run **by hand** as I asked — 1017 cases. Four PREREQUISITE-NOT-MET gates were **satisfied** by building the named packages, not recorded as red. `check-test-completeness` NOT MEASURED by its own words.

⭐ And `pnpm lint` is a **proven-empty narrowing with three pieces of evidence** — population read from ESLint's own flat config (all four files reported ignored), `--format json` counts, and an invariance argument (no `projectService` ⇒ type-aware linting off ⇒ this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file). ⛔ Not a skipped run dressed as a narrowing.

**Filed:** #13661 — two code comments still describing the elevation gate L4 retired, one of which **ships in the types package declarations**. ⛔ Comment-only, no behaviour defect; unassigned and ungraded.

### Landing

⛔ Not governed (`content/docs/**` only — and outside epic #12243's declared slice of it) and ⛔ not clause ②. ⇒ **armable once CI converges.**
